title: Design and Analysis of Analog ICs in Advanced CMOS Technologies
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg;Not for students who have taken ELEG5723
description: This course focuses on the design and analysis of analog integrated circuits in advanced CMOS technologies. Students will explore the principles and techniques for designing key analog circuit building blocks, including operational amplifiers, comparators, voltage and current references, switched-capacitor circuits, current-mode circuits, and continuous-time filters. The course also examines A/D and D/A converters, covering parallel, serial, algorithmic, and oversampling architectures. Extensive circuit simulations are conducted using state-of-the-art tools such as Cadence/SPECTRE, enabling students to gain hands-on experience with modern design workflows. Mandatory group projects on designing analog IC will be included, with final reports and presentations.
outcome: After finishing this course, students will be able to- analyze and design CMOS analog IC building blocks, like operational transconductance amplifiers and comparators.- analyze, design and characterize basic CMOS data converters of different type, including flash, successive approximation, pipeline, and oversampling types.
syllabus: Review of transistor models; Performance metrics Passive components; mismatch model; Fundamental performance limits Power/accuracy trade-off: SAR ADCs as examples Pipelined ADC: requirements on OTAs Basic one- and two-transistor amplifiers   Noise and mismatch of elementary stages One-stage OTAs Two-stage OTAs Fully-differential OTAs Bias and references Comparators Switched-capacitor circuits Overview of other A/D and D/A converters
required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
recommended_readings: Gray/Hurst/Lewis/Meyer, Analysis and Design of Analog Integrated Circuits, 4th edition, Wiley, 2001. Allen/Holberg, CMOS Analog Circuit Design, Oxford, 2002. Laker/Sansen, Design of Analog Integrated Circuits and Systems, McGraw-Hill, 1994. Johns/Martin, Analog Integrated Circuit Design, Wiley, 1997. Razavi, Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits, McGraw-Hill, 2001. (Recommended to buy) Y. Tsividis, Mixed Analog-Digital VLSI Devices and Technology, McGraw-Hill, 1996 Baker, CMOS Mixed-Signal Circuit Design, Wiley, 2002.

title: Digital Signal Processing IC Design
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg;Not for students who have taken ELEG5758
description: This course focuses on the design methodologies for VLSI circuits implementing digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms across a variety of applications. It introduces architectural optimization techniques such as pipelining, retiming, unfolding, folding, and systolic arrays to enhance speed, reduce power consumption, or minimize size. Students will also learn hardware description languages (HDL) and apply them to design and implement DSP systems. Through practical sessions providing hands-on experience in VLSI-based DSP architecture design and implementation.
outcome: 1. Use signal diagram to describe digital signal processing algorithms. 2. Understand different architectural transforms to optimize a VLSI DSP circuit for speed, power consumption or size. 3. Understand a Hardware Description Language and has the ability to use the HDL to design VLSI DSP circuits. 4. Gain the experience of using FPGA Design Tools
syllabus: This course deals with methodologies to design VLSI circuits for DSP algorithms used in a wide range of signal processing applications. Architectural techniques to optimize for speed, power consumption or size include pipelining, retiming, unfolding, folding and systolic array. The course also introduces a hardware description language, and shows the use of HDL to design a specific digital processing example. Practical will be arranged for students to gain first hand experience of designing and implementing DSP algorithms.
required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
recommended_readings: VLSI Digital Signal Processing Systems Design and Implementation by Keshab K. Parhi  Digital VLSI Systems Design A Design Manual for Implementation of Projects on FPGAs and ASICs using Verilog by Seetharaman Ramacandran

title: Smart Power IC Design
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg;Not for students who have taken ELEG5726
description: This course explores the design, simulation, and measurement techniques for smart power integrated circuits. Students will study essential building blocks such as bandgap voltage references, linear regulators, switched-mode regulators and charge pumps. The course also introduces circuit layout design and floor planning, providing a comprehensive understanding of power IC design. Through exercises and simulations, students will gain hands-on experience with modern methodologies used in the development of smart power circuit solutions. Mandatory exercises on designing power converters will be included. During the exercises, students will apply their learned theories and concepts within the design process, engage professional discussions with course instructor and TAs, and understand implications of design choices.
outcome: By the end of the course, students should be able to-        Have an overall picture of the history, progress, and importance of power-management circuits.-        Understand the principle of operation of typical voltage regulators-        Perform circuit designs of voltage reference, linear regulator and switching-mode power converter.-        Understand the design tradeoffs of the specifications.
syllabus: 1. Introduction: Overviews of Applications of Power-Management ICs, Reasons on Separated Power and Voltage Regulation, Voltage Reference, Linear Regulator, Switched-Mode Regulator and Charge Pump.2. Voltage reference: Requirements of a Voltage Reference, Bandgap Voltage Reference – Basics, Bandgap Voltage Reference – Theory, Design Considerations – BJT Ratio, Base Resistance, Base Current and Resistor, Error-Amplifier-Based Bandgap, Power-Supply Rejection Ratio, Line Transient Response, Load Transient Response, Startup and Stability, Measurement.3. Linear regulator: Concept of Linear Regulator, Structure of Low-Dropout Regulator (LDO), Working Principle and Power Efficiency, Dropout Voltage and Power-Transistor Sizing, Load Regulation, Line Regulation, Temperature Coefficient, Load Transient Response, Output Noise, Power-Supply Rejection Ratio, Stability and Compensation, LDO Design Dependence & Output Accuracy, Circuit Implementation, Floor planning and Measurement.4. Switched-Mode Regulator: Trade-offs between different types of regulators, Operation Principle of Switched-Mode Regulator, Asynchronous vs Synchronous Regulator, Switched-Inductor Regulator with Ideal Components, CCM vs DCM Operation, Available Inductors, Available Capacitors, Output Ripple with non-ideal component, Efficiency of Switched-mode Regulator, Important Waveforms of a Buck Regulator, Other Switched-Inductor Regulators, Efficiency as a function of MOS Switch Resistance, Dead-time Control, Turn-on and –off Transition, Dead-time Circuit, Buffer Design to Drive Large Capacitive Load, Feedback Control, Simple Voltage-Mode Feedback Control, Hysteretic Voltage-Mode Control, Hysteretic Comparator, Voltage Comparator Design, PWM (Pulse-Width-Modulation) Control, PWM Generator, Clock & Ramp Generator, Set-Dominant RS Flip-Flop, Error Amplifier and Compensator, Dominant Pole Compensation, Layout Floor Planning and Power Transistor Connection.5. Charge pump: Concept of Charge Pump, Voltage Doubler, Voltage Divider, Voltage Inverter, Voltage Tripler, 1.5 Charge Pump, Output Voltage and Efficiency of a Voltage Doubler, Switches and Gate Drives of a Voltage Doubler and Applying the Deadtime Circuit to Voltage Doubler.
required_readings: -        P. Gray, P.J. Hurst, S.H. Lewis and R.G. Meyer, Analysis and Design of Analog Integrated Circuits, 4th ed., Wiley, 2001.-        B. Razavi, Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits, McGraw Hill, 2001.-        P.E. Allen and D.R. Holberg, CMOS Analog Circuit Design, 2nd ed., Oxford, 2002.-        D. Johns and K. Martin, Analog Integrated Circuit Design, Wiley, 1997.-        A. Hastings, The Art of Analog Layout, New Jersey: Prentice Hall, 2001.

title: Advanced Semiconductor Packaging
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits
description: This subject aims to train students with the fundamental knowledge of microelectronic and power electronic packaging technologies, including concepts, electrical design, structural & thermal design, material selection, process development, test and failure analysis, with the focus on the understanding of mainstream packaging technologies for high-power & high-frequency related applications. Tutorials can be arranged to ensure the students with hand-on experience on the mainstream design software and understand the fabrication process of electronic packages/modules in industry.The content of this course is composed of seven parts: 1) Mainstream microelectronics packaging format & process; 2) Mainstream power electronics packaging format & process; 3) Fundamentals of thermal management, mechanics & reliability; 4) Electrical, thermal and mechanical co-design considerations with case studies; 5) Modelling and simulation of mainstream electronic packages; 6) Chiplet design and heterogeneous integration packaging; 7) Techniques for failure analysis.
outcome: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:1. Understand mainstream microelectronics & power electronics packaging format & process;2. Understand the fundamentals of thermal management, mechanics & reliability;3. Understand the principles of reliability tests & failure analysis techniques;4. Use mainstream EDA tools in the industry to design and simulate the performance of electronics packages.

title: Advanced RF Circuit Design and Systems
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits;Not for students who have taken ELEG5732
description: This course explores advanced concepts in RF technologies and system design. It covers RF circuit design methodologies, the use of microwave CAD tools, state-of-the-art measurement techniques, and RF power amplifier design. Students will study RF transceiver architectures, noise analysis, system linearity, and their implications for RF performance. The course also delves into modern wireless communication technologies, providing a foundation for cutting-edge RF system development.
outcome: By the end of the course, students will be able to-        Have a basic understanding of some modern wireless communication systems and technologies.-        Understand the basic operating principles of RF circuits.-        Design, simulate, construct and conduct measurement of RF circuits.-        Perform the design of various RF amplifiers for different applications.-        Understand the design and implementation of various RF transceiver architectures.       -        Understand the noise and linearity issues relating to RF systems & applications.
syllabus: Introduction to RF technologies; RF circuit design methodologies; Microwave CAD tools; Measurement techniques; RF power amplifier design; RF transceiver architecture; Noise & Linearity study of RF systems; Modern wireless technologies.
required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
recommended_readings: Text:L. Bretchko, “RF Circuit Design Theory and Applications”, Prentice Hall, 2000. Reference book:1. D. M. Pozar, “Microwave and RF Design of Wireless Systems”, John Wiley, 2005.2. M. M. Radmanesh, “Radio Frequency & Microwave Electronics illustrated”, Prentice Hall, 2001.3. B. Razavi, “RF Microelectronics”, Prentice Hall, 1998.

title: CMOS Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits Design
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits
description: This subject aims to train students with the advanced knowledge of radio frequency (RF) integrated circuit design in the advanced CMOS technology, including design and analysis of widely-used RF transceiver architectures and circuits. The student will get hands-on experience to design and analyze RF integrated circuits and get familiar with the complete design flow from circuit design, layout design and parasitic parameters extraction.The content of this course is composed of seven parts: 1)RF passive circuits and matching networks; 2) Noise and nonlinearity in RF system; 3) Communication system and standard; 4) RF transceiver architecture; 5) RF transceiver calibration; 6) RF module circuit design; 7) Introduction to mmWave IC. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge in physics, semiconductor device and integrated circuits.

title: Digital VLSI Circuit Design and Introduction to AI IC
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits;Not for students who have taken ELEG5764 and ELEG5765
description: Core curriculum of digital IC (Integrated Circuit) design, which provides the students with essential knowledge and techniques to design digital IC chip and further introduction to AI (Artificial Intelligence) IC. In this course the students can learn the following contents: 1) Mechanism of CMOSFET transistor; 2) IC elements: Logic gates, latch and FF; 3) Combinational and sequential circuits; 4) Verilog-HDL hardware description language for IC design: Syntax, example, and testbench; 5) Analysis of circuit delay, performance, timing and protocol; 6) Industry EDA tool software for IC design; 7) Number system in IC domain: Integer, floating-point number; 8) Design of common circuit blocks; 9) Basic types of data bus standard and communication protocol; 10) Overview of AI algorithm and computation; 11) Fundamental AI circuit design; 12) Architecture of AI IC.
outcome: 1. Understand the working mechanism of CMOSFET transistor. 2. Understand the logic gates, latch and FF composed of transistors and can design new circuit elements. 3. Understand combinational and sequential circuits and can design circuits with required function. 4. Understand the syntax of Verilog-HDL and can design circuit and the corresponding testbench with Verilog. 5. Analyze the delay, performance, timing and protocol of IC. 6. Make use of industry EDA tool software to design IC. 7. Understand the number system in IC domain: Integer, floating-point number. 8. Design common IC modules. 9. Understand basic data bus standard and communication protocol, and can implement them in IC. 10. Understand basic AI algorithms and computation. 11. Design fundamental AI circuits. 12. Understand the architecture of AI IC.
syllabus: Introduction to IC industry CMOSFET transistor, logic gates, latch, FF Combinational and sequential circuit Number system in IC Verilog syntax: 1 Verilog syntax: 2 Verilog testbench EDA tool software Common IC modules Data bus standard Communication protocol AI algorithm and computation AI circuit design Architecture of AI IC
required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
recommended_readings: 1. Samir Palnitkar, “Verilog HDL: A Guide to Digital Design and Synthesis”.2. Michael D. Ciletti, “Advanced Digital Design with the Verilog HDL”.3. Kishore Mishra, “Advanced Chip Design: Practical Examples in Verilog”.4. David A. Patterson, et al., “Computer Organization and Design”.5. 夏宇聞，“Verilog數字系統設計教程”。

title: Mixed-signal Integrated Circuit Design
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits;Not for students who have taken ELEG5769
description: This subject aims to train students with the advanced knowledge of mixed-signal integrated circuit design in the advanced CMOS technology, including design and analysis of the circuit and theory of switch capacitor circuit, analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and digital-to-analog converter (DAC). The student will get hands-on experience to design and analyze advanced mixed-signal integrated circuits and complete design flow from circuit design, layout design and parasitic parameters extraction.The content of this course is composed of eight parts: 1) ADC/DAC fundamentals; 2) switch capacitor circuit; 3) SAR ADC; 4) pipelined ADC; 5) interleaved ADC; 6) sigma-delta ADC; 7) high resolution DAC; 8) high-speed DAC. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge in physics, semiconductor device and integrated circuits.

title: RISC-V Integrated Circuit
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg;Not for students who have taken ELEG5763
description: This course explores the principles of processor design using the RISC-V instruction set architecture, an open and customizable standard driving innovation in modern computing. It covers the fundamentals of processor design, including a basic pipelined implementation of RISC-V. Students will learn performance enhancement techniques such as cache optimization, instruction-level parallelism, and data-level parallelism. Students will build a strong foundation in processor design and performance optimization for diverse real-world applications
outcome: Understand the basic concept of processor design Understand RISC-V ISA and appreciate the merit of different control implementations Use memory organization to increase performance Use different levels of parallelism to increase performance Gain ability to configure a RISC-V
syllabus: Basic Processor DesignRISC-V ISARISC-V Pipelined DatapathInstruction HazardsMemory Organization and CacheVirtual MemoryInstruction Level ParallelismData Level Parallelism

title: Artificial Intelligence IC Design
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits;Not for students who have taken ELEG5764
description: With the rapid development and increasingly application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology, specific AI Integrated Circuits (IC) are required to provide powerful and efficient computing capability, which drives the needs in market for types of AI IC suitable for different application situation. Therefore, this course intends to provide the enrolled students with the typical technology, system architecture and design methodology for AI IC design. Moreover, software tool chains are also introduced. This course is to support and enable the students with improved capability to design AI IC.The content of this course is composed of the following sections: 1) Fundamentals of AI and typical algorithms; 2) Technology and system architecture of AI IC, as well as design methodology considering algorithm, software and hardware; 3) Software tool chains related to the application of AI IC; 4) Emerging semiconductor devices, computing modality, circuit design, system architecture, requirement and trend; 5) Practice of AI IC design; 6) GPGPU; 7) CUDA. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge in digital IC design.
outcome: 1. Understand the typical algorithms for AI computing. 2. Understand the design techniques and representative architectures of AI IC. 3. Understand the Domain-Specific Architecture (DSA) design methodology including algorithm, hardware and software. 4. Understand the software tools for AI IC. 5. Understand emerging semiconductor devices, system architecture, requirement and trend. 6. Obtain practical experience of system development including requirement analysis, algorithm optimization, IC architecture and module design. 7. Understand the architecture and application of GPGPU. 8. Understand the principal and application of CUDA.
syllabus: Introduction to artificial intelligence IC Essentials of AI algorithms and Computer Architecture Characteristics of AI computing Architectures of AI IC – Overview Architectures of AI IC – Operator Architectures of AI IC – Data flow Architectures of AI IC – Advance Design methodology of AI IC GPGPU CUDA Tool chains of AI IC Emerging devices, architectures and trend Compute in Memory Advanced topics
required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
recommended_readings: 1. David A. Patterson, et al., “Computer Organization and Design”.2. Bert Moons, et al., “Embedded Deep Learning – Algorithms, architectures and Circuits”.3. Tor M. Aamodt, etc., “General-Purpose Graphics Processor Architecture”.4. 尹首一，“人工智能芯片設計”。5. 陳云霽，“智能計算系統”。6. 梁曉峣, “昇騰AI處理器 – 架構與編程”.  7. 景乃鋒，“通用圖形處理器設計”。8. Alfred V. Aho, et al., “Compilers - Principles, Techniques and Tools”.9. R. Krishnamoorthi, “Quantizing Deep Convolutional Networks for Efficient Inference”.10. M. Li, et al., “The Deep Learning Compiler: A Comprehensive Survey”.

title: Digital Automotive IC Design
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits;Not for students who have taken ELEG5765
description: The emerging intelligence of automotive vehicles, robots, unmanned aerial vehicles and industry equipment requires increasingly powerful computing capability embedded in vehicles, which motivates the eager demand for automotive Integrated Circuit (IC). Automotive IC is required to implement the functions needed by the electronic systems in vehicles and equipment, and to be with such characteristics as high reliability and robustness. This course intends to provide for the enrolled students with the knowledge of automotive IC, including the characteristics, design, related software and application. Further more, such advanced knowledges as AXI bus, SoC (System on Chip), high level of IC design and verification language SystemVerilog, UVM (Universal Verification Methodology) will also be provided, which is required for complicated IC in other domains besides vehicles. The students can therefore be with knowledge and design capability for both automotive IC and universal complicated IC.The content of this course is composed of the following parts: 1) Electrical and electronic architecture of vehicle; 2) Particulars of automotive IC; 3) CAN (Controller Area Network); 4) Design methodology of digital automotive IC; 5) AXI bus; 6) Hardware and software of SoC (System on Chip); 7) SystemVerilog; 8) UVM. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge of digital IC design.

title: Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits Internship
requirements: For students in MSc Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits
description: This course is designed to allow students to acquire a basic understanding and the skills of the practical aspects of the Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits Internship profession. During the internship, the student must attach to a company in a study-related position for no less than 12 weeks. The student will have an academic supervisor (as primary supervisor) and an industry co-supervisor from the company, both have the expertise to provide advice to the student. To be qualified for award of the subject credit, the student must submit a report summarizing the internship experience at the end of the internship. Additional presentation may be required by the hosting company.The internship should normally take place in the summer term after a student has finished the first two semesters of studies. Part-time students can decide to undertake the internship in the summer term of either the first or second year of studies. Students are recommended to seek the Professor-in-Charge's comment on potential internship opportunities before enrolling in the course.
outcome: At the end of the course of studies, a student should be able to1. Have a good understanding and appreciate the characteristics of a Microelectronics and Integrated CircuitsInternshipwork environment, including employer expectation, management structure of a team, industrial standards and practices, trends and common issues in the Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits, etc.;2. Carry out basic duties in a Microelectronics and Integrated Circuits Internship work environment;3. Exhibit good etiquette in the workplace;4. Work independently as well as in a team environment; and5. Communicate effectively and efficiently with peers, supervisors and possibly also clients.
